items.title: Philippines’ VP Duterte Posts Bail, Says She Fears for Her Life
items.description: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail for a criminal case accusing her of threatening to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. She said she fears for her own life.

items.title: Europe’s Wealth Managers Are Turning Their Backs on Stock Rally
items.description: More European wealth managers have turned pessimistic on the region’s stocks, taking the view that this year’s rally is likely to falter while markets in the US and developing countries power ahead.

items.title: Malaysia’s PAS Party Wants Nationwide Gambling License Review
items.description: Parti Islam Se-Malaysia, which leads the country’s main opposition bloc, said the government should review existing gambling licenses and stop giving new ones, its latest effort to curb social ills.

items.title: HK’s Lee Says City to Expand Offshore Yuan Usage in 5-Year Plan
items.description: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee said the city’s first five-year plan will focus on areas including expanding offshore yuan usage and cross-border investment with the mainland.

items.title: Bloom Energy, Illumina, Everpure to Join S&P 500 This Month
items.description: Bloom Energy Corp., Illumina Inc. and Everpure Inc. will join the S&P 500 in the latest quarterly rebalance, S&P Dow Jones Indices said Friday.

items.description: The global bond selloff is proving no wrecking ball for Wall Street, repricing the cost of money without setting off the usual scramble out of risk assets.

items.title: Emerging Currencies Cap Longest Winning Streak Since 2007
items.description: An index for emerging-market currencies rose for a 10th successive week, its longest winning streak since 2007, even as a blowout US jobs report briefly jolted global markets on Friday.
